title: Real Estate Letter of Intent (Non-Binding)
summary: Outline the key deal terms for a property before negotiating a full purchase contract. Mostly non-binding.
useWhen: Making an offer on investment, commercial or multifamily property where a detailed purchase agreement will follow.
watchOuts: Courts sometimes enforce LOIs as contracts when they look complete and the parties act on them. Keep the non-binding language clear, and keep binding terms short.
Exclusivity ('no-shop') and confidentiality are usually the only binding terms. Keep exclusivity short.
An LOI is not a substitute for a purchase agreement or state-required disclosures.

variables.label: Buyer name
variables.help: Buyer or buying entity, 'and/or assigns' if applicable.

variables.label: Payment terms
variables.help: Cash, new loan, seller financing, subject-to, or a combination.

variables.label: Due diligence period (days)
variables.help: After the purchase agreement is signed.

variables.label: Documents the seller will provide
variables.default: Rent roll, leases, trailing 12 months of operating statements, utility bills, tax bills, service contracts, existing surveys and environmental reports.
variables.help: What the buyer needs to review.

variables.label: Contingencies
variables.default: Satisfactory due diligence, financing on terms acceptable to buyer, clear title.

variables.label: Seller agrees to exclusivity?
variables.help: Seller stops marketing for a short period.

variables.label: LOI expires
variables.help: Date the seller must sign by.

sections.title: 1. Purpose
sections.body: Date: {{loi_date}}. This letter summarizes the main terms on which {{buyer_name}} ("Buyer") proposes to buy {{property_address}} (the "Property") from {{seller_name}} ("Seller"). The parties intend to negotiate a definitive purchase agreement.

sections.title: 2. Proposed terms
3. Not binding
sections.body: **Except for the sections titled Confidentiality, Exclusivity (if included), Costs and Governing law, this letter is not a binding contract.** It creates no obligation to buy or sell, and no obligation to negotiate further. Either party may stop negotiations at any time for any reason. A binding agreement exists only when both parties sign a definitive purchase agreement.

sections.title: 4. Confidentiality
sections.body: Each party will keep the terms of this letter and any non-public information it receives about the Property confidential, except for disclosure to its advisers, lenders and investors who need to know.

sections.title: 5. Exclusivity
sections.body: For {{exclusivity_days}} days after Seller signs, Seller will not market the Property, solicit offers or negotiate with anyone else about a sale.

sections.title: 6. Costs
sections.body: Each party pays its own costs of negotiating this letter and the purchase agreement.

sections.title: 7. Governing law and expiration
sections.body: The binding sections are governed by the law of {{governing_state}}. This letter expires if not signed by Seller by {{expires}}.

sections.title: Signatures
sections.body:
Acknowledged and agreed, including the binding sections:

**Prospective buyer** — {{buyer_name}}

[[sig:buyer]]

Printed name: [[name:buyer]]
Title (if signing for a company): [[text:buyer:Title]]
Date: [[date:buyer]]

**Property owner** — {{seller_name}}

[[sig:seller]]

Printed name: [[name:seller]]
Title (if signing for a company): [[text:seller:Title]]
Date: [[date:seller]]

disclaimer: This is a starting template from the Massless open contract library. It is not legal advice, and using it does not create an attorney-client relationship. Laws vary by state and change over time. Have a licensed attorney in your state review it before you sign. Real estate contracts carry state-specific disclosure, licensing, closing and recording rules. If a real estate licensee is involved, the licensee may be required to use state-promulgated or approved forms instead of this one (for example in Texas and Colorado). Deeds, mortgages and deeds of trust usually must be notarized and recorded; an electronic signature on this document does not record anything.

sources.title: Pryor Cashman: The enforceability of letters of intent
